---
title: "Center Buildout Capacity"
subtitle: "Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown, and The Point"
---

## Purpose

Estimate additional housing units and jobs at full buildout for three WCV
centers:

- **Daybreak** and **Saratoga Springs Downtown**: from REMM-forecast
  post-2025 development, applying each center's median dwelling-unit-per-acre
  and employment-density (FAR + job-space) assumptions to the forecast
  residential / commercial-employment development mix.
- **The Point**: from the development schedule the Point team has provided
  directly, rather than from REMM.

Spatial joins, filtering, and aggregation below run in geopandas/pandas.
The base-year parcels come from `remm_base_year_data.gdb`, which is cached
as GeoParquet on first run (see below) so later runs just read that instead
of re-parsing the FileGDB.

## Centers of interest

Single ordered list to extend if more centers are added later.
`center_boundaries` is fetched in full from the REST service (no
server-side `where`), so adding a center here doesn't require touching
`sources.yml` or re-fetching -- just delete `_data/processed/centers.parquet`
to force it to rebuild with the updated list. Subsets below are index
slices into this same list: `[0:2]` for the two REMM-method centers
(Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown), `[2:3]` for The Point.

Every `gpd.read_file()` call below passes an OGR SQL `where` built straight
from that list, restricted to "Urban Center" polygons (drops The Point's
separate "Employment District" polygon, since every center in scope for
this analysis is its Urban Center polygon).

```{python}
CENTERS_OF_INTEREST = ["Daybreak", "Saratoga Springs Downtown", "The Point"]
```

## Load center boundaries

```{python}
from gis_adhoc_analyses.layer_cache import ensure_layers
import geopandas as gpd

L = ensure_layers(["center_boundaries"])
centers_preview = gpd.read_file(
    L["center_boundaries"],
    where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
)
centers_preview[["CenterName", "CenterType", "City", "DwellingPerAcre", "NonResFAR"]]
```

```{python}
centers_preview.explore(column="CenterName", tooltip=["CenterName", "CenterType", "City"], legend=False)
```

## REMM parcels: load and cache as parquet

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "buildings_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "buildings_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "buildings_2055.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

# one-time read of the two vector sources, cached as GeoParquet so later runs
# don't re-parse the FileGDB or re-fetch the REST layer.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels", columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres"])
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(
        L["center_boundaries"],
        columns=["CenterName", "CenterType"],
        where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
    )
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

if not paths["buildings_2055_parquet"].exists():
    buildings_full = pd.read_pickle(paths["buildings_2055_pkl"]).reset_index()
    # 'note' mixes strings with an int 0 sentinel (no dedicated null), which pyarrow
    # can't write as a single column type -- cast to string so every row survives
    # as-is (0 -> "0") rather than dropping columns to sidestep the type error.
    buildings_full["note"] = buildings_full["note"].astype(str)
    buildings_full.to_parquet(paths["buildings_2055_parquet"])

if not paths["progression_2055_parquet"].exists():
    pd.read_pickle(paths["progression_2055_pkl"]).to_parquet(paths["progression_2055_parquet"])

parcels = gpd.read_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])
centers = gpd.read_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"]).to_crs(parcels.crs)
```

## Parcels within each center

Centroid-in-polygon join (not a straight intersection) so a parcel
straddling a center boundary is assigned to exactly one center, not
double-counted.

```{python}
parcel_centroids = parcels.set_geometry(parcels.geometry.centroid)

parcels_in_centers = gpd.sjoin(
    parcel_centroids, centers[["CenterName", "geometry"]], predicate="within", how="inner"
)[["parcel_id", "parcel_acres", "CenterName"]]

parcels_in_centers.groupby("CenterName").agg(
    n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum")
)
```

## Daybreak & Saratoga Springs: REMM developable land

Follows the original pseudocode directly: filter the 2055 buildings table
(`run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl`, one row per *building*) to parcels
within our two centers, keep buildings with `year_built > 2025`, take the
unique parcel ids from that, then sum `parcel_acres` for those parcels.

An earlier version of this shortcut off the parcel-level
`parcel_progression_metrics` table instead, since it already carries a
single `year_built` per parcel. That's only valid if every building on a
parcel always shares the same year/type -- checked directly: 162 parcels
regionwide have more than one building, 2 of them are in our two centers,
and in both cases the buildings on that parcel happened to share the same
`year_built`. That was a coincidence of this dataset, not something the
data guarantees in general, so this now filters at the building level as
originally specified rather than relying on it holding elsewhere.

```{python}
buildings_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"],
    columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "residential_units", "job_spaces"],
)

our_parcels = parcels_in_centers[parcels_in_centers["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)]
buildings_in_centers = buildings_2055.merge(
    our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id"
)

post_2025_parcel_ids = buildings_in_centers.loc[
    buildings_in_centers["year_built"] > 2025, "parcel_id"
].unique()

developable_land = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids)]
    .groupby("CenterName")
    .agg(n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum"))
    .reset_index()
)
developable_land
```

### Forecast development mix and buildout capacity

Daybreak and Saratoga Springs Downtown only -- The Point's buildout comes
from its own development schedule, not this REMM-based estimate.

```{python}
task2_parcel_ids = our_parcels.loc[
    our_parcels["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2])
    & our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids),
    "parcel_id",
]
```

**Step 1 -- residential : jobs ratio.** Sum `residential_units` and
`job_spaces` from `parcel_progression_metrics` for the same post-2025
developable parcels identified above. These two fields were checked
directly against the buildings table and are reliable per-parcel sums
across all of a parcel's buildings (unlike `year_built`, which only
reflects one representative building) -- see note above.

```{python}
progression_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["progression_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "residential_units", "job_spaces"]
)

dev_mix = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(task2_parcel_ids)][["parcel_id", "CenterName"]]
    .merge(progression_2055, on="parcel_id")
    .groupby("CenterName")[["residential_units", "job_spaces"]]
    .sum()
)
dev_mix["res_share"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / (dev_mix["residential_units"] + dev_mix["job_spaces"])
dev_mix["nonres_share"] = 1 - dev_mix["res_share"]
dev_mix
```

**Step 2 -- allocate each center's developable acreage by that ratio.**

```{python}
acreage_allocation = developable_land.set_index("CenterName").loc[
    CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2], ["total_acres"]
].join(dev_mix[["res_share", "nonres_share"]])
acreage_allocation["res_acres"] = acreage_allocation["total_acres"] * acreage_allocation["res_share"]
acreage_allocation["nonres_acres"] = acreage_allocation["total_acres"] * acreage_allocation["nonres_share"]
acreage_allocation
```

**Step 3 -- median capacity assumptions.** Per Josh's guidance, "median"
means the midpoint of the standard planning range for the center's type
(all three of ours are "Urban Center": FAR 0.75-4.0, DUA 20-100) -- not a
statistical median computed from the parcels table's own `max_far`/`max_dua`
columns. The `DwellingPerAcre`/`NonResFAR` fields on the REST-cached center
layer already carry each center's own range string, so this parses those
directly.

```{python}
def range_midpoint(range_str):
    lo, hi = range_str.split("-")
    return (float(lo) + float(hi)) / 2


capacities = centers_preview.set_index("CenterName").loc[
    CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2], ["DwellingPerAcre", "NonResFAR"]
]
capacities["median_dua"] = capacities["DwellingPerAcre"].apply(range_midpoint)
capacities["median_far"] = capacities["NonResFAR"].apply(range_midpoint)
capacities
```

**Step 4 -- sqft-per-job assumption**, from each center's own post-2025
non-residential buildings. `sqft_per_job` turns out to be a fixed constant
per building `general_type` region-wide (Office 633, Retail 374, Industrial
975, ...), so taking the median here reflects each center's forecast
non-res building mix rather than sampling noise.

```{python}
buildings_full = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "sqft_per_job"]
).merge(our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id")

nonres_post_2025 = buildings_full[
    (buildings_full["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST[0:2]))
    & (buildings_full["year_built"] > 2025)
    & ~buildings_full["general_type"].isin(["SF Residential", "MF Residential"])
]
sqft_per_job = nonres_post_2025.groupby("CenterName")["sqft_per_job"].median().rename("sqft_per_job")
sqft_per_job
```

**Step 5 -- combine into full-buildout capacity.**

```{python}
SQFT_PER_ACRE = 43_560

capacity = acreage_allocation.join(capacities[["median_dua", "median_far"]]).join(sqft_per_job)
capacity["housing_units"] = capacity["res_acres"] * capacity["median_dua"]
capacity["nonres_sqft"] = capacity["nonres_acres"] * capacity["median_far"] * SQFT_PER_ACRE
capacity["jobs"] = capacity["nonres_sqft"] / capacity["sqft_per_job"]
capacity[["total_acres", "res_acres", "nonres_acres", "housing_units", "jobs"]]
```
